description:
Maintainer request (2026-07-28): chat is laggy on CPU; offload some tensor ops to a wgpu kernel when resources allow. Must stay compiling cleanly on Termux, and the hybrid CPU/wgpu path must be compared properly against llama.cpp.

STATE OF PLAY, measured not assumed:
* crates/kopitiam-gpu already exists (AID-0037): wgpu + pollster + bytemuck, a GpuContext, an Executor with a GPU->CPU fallback cascade, and exactly ONE op - vector_add. It is NOT wired into kopitiam-tensor or kopitiam-runtime at all, so nothing in inference touches the GPU today.
* TERMUX COMPILES CLEAN ALREADY. 'cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android -p kopitiam-gpu' succeeds in ~30s; wgpu pulls ndk-sys/jni-sys/wgpu-core-deps-windows-linux-android and checks green. So a build-time gate is NOT required for Termux to compile. A gate would buy smaller/faster Termux builds (skipping the whole wgpu tree) rather than fixing a breakage - worth doing for that reason, but the premise that it currently fails to compile does not hold.

WHAT TO OFFLOAD, in cost order: the matmuls dominate. attn q/k/v/o projections, the MLP gate/up/down, and the output projection - that is where a 360M spends nearly all its time. probs@V and q@K^T are next. Elementwise ops (silu, rms_norm, add) are not worth a round trip on their own; they are only worth it if the tensors are already resident on the GPU, which means the real win needs a resident-tensor design rather than op-by-op offload with a copy each way.

HARD SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT - read bd-b9x first. Our CPU forward pass currently DISAGREES with llama.cpp, and the gap grows with prompt length (bd-b9x, P0, confirmed against a locally built llama.cpp on the same .gguf). Offloading now would (a) make a wrong answer arrive faster, and (b) destroy the ability to validate: a GPU-vs-llama.cpp comparison would inherit the existing error, so a genuine GPU kernel bug could not be told apart from bd-b9x. Fix bd-b9x, THEN the three-way GPU/CPU/llama.cpp comparison the maintainer asked for is actually meaningful.

HOW TO VALIDATE when the time comes: docs/REFERENCE-ORACLE.md documents building and driving llama-completion/llama-tokenize from the vendored clone, and the variables that must be controlled (greedy both sides, -ctk/-ctv f32, the -f vs -e -p trailing-newline trap, KOPITIAM_FORCE_F32_WEIGHTS). Every GPU kernel additionally gets the treatment the CPU ops already have: compared element-wise against a hand-computed reference at REAL attention shapes, not just 'it ran'.

Also worth knowing before designing: on Termux there is usually no usable Vulkan driver, so the cascade will fall back to CPU there anyway. The lag the maintainer feels on Windows is the case that benefits.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
PROGRESS, commit ce74f2b1be: the wgpu matmul kernel exists, is correctness-checked against its CPU twin at real transformer shapes, and - more importantly - is MEASURED. The measurements change the plan.

MEASURED on Intel integrated GPU vs 14 CPU cores, SmolLM2-360M real shapes, timings INCLUDE upload+readback:
  decode  attn q/o     (1 tok)   cpu   443us   gpu 1.88ms   0.24x   LOSS
  decode  mlp gate/up  (1 tok)   cpu  1.28ms   gpu 3.20ms   0.40x   LOSS
  decode  mlp down     (1 tok)   cpu  1.29ms   gpu 2.86ms   0.45x   LOSS
  decode  output head  (1 tok)   cpu 25.67ms   n/a - exceeds binding limit
  prefill attn q/o    (33 tok)   cpu 12.89ms   gpu 3.72ms   3.46x   WIN
  prefill mlp gate/up (33 tok)   cpu 40.83ms   gpu 7.77ms   5.26x   WIN

CONCLUSION: do NOT offload uniformly. A decode step is one row of activations and cannot amortise moving a weight matrix; a 33-token prefill does 33x the arithmetic against the same upload and wins outright. Offloading everything - the obvious reading of the original request - would make chat 2-4x SLOWER.

REMAINING WORK, in value order:
1. OUTPUT HEAD, QUANTIZED + RESIDENT. It is 49152x960 and costs 25.67ms per token on CPU - more than every other decode matmul combined, so it IS the chat lag. It cannot go to the GPU as f32 at all: 188MB against this adapter's 128MB max_storage_buffer_binding_size. Keeping it Q8_0 on the device is ~47MB, which fits. This needs a q8 matmul kernel (dequantise in-shader) plus residency. Highest value by a wide margin.
2. PREFILL OFFLOAD. Wire matmul_nt into kopitiam-runtime's linear() for the seq>1 case only, guarded on Executor::has_gpu(). Straightforward given the kernel exists; worth 3.5-5.3x on prompt ingestion.
3. RESIDENT WEIGHTS for decode. Upload each weight once at model load. Ownership/lifetime design question - a GpuLinear owning its device buffer - deliberately not smuggled in with the first kernel.
4. TILED KERNEL. The current shader is one invocation per output element with a plain dot product. Shared-memory tiling would raise the prefill win further, but it is a multiplier on (2), not a prerequisite.

BUG FIXED EN ROUTE, found by benchmarking rather than review: wgpu treats an over-limit storage binding as a validation error and PANICS, aborting the process instead of returning Err for the cascade. The output head triggers it exactly. matmul_nt_gpu now checks device limits up front and refuses with InvalidInput so the Executor falls to CPU; regression test constructs a weight one row past whatever the local adapter's limit is, so it holds on any device.

TERMUX: confirmed again - cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android passes. No gating was ever needed for compilation. Note Termux typically has no usable Vulkan driver, so the cascade lands on CPU there regardless; the lag this work addresses is the desktop case.

COMPARISON DISCIPLINE (maintainer's instruction): the hybrid path must be compared to llama.cpp, and that is now possible - bd-b9x is fixed, so our CPU forward pass agrees with llama.cpp. docs/REFERENCE-ORACLE.md documents the oracle. Any offload landing in the forward pass must be checked three ways: GPU vs our CPU twin element-wise, and end-to-end output vs llama.cpp.

title: gpu: offload the matmuls to wgpu (blocked on bd-b9x), keep Termux builds clean
